decision: Stock is allocated as available-to-promise per channel, fed by stock.reserved events
why: Site, app, marketplace and stores sell the same units at the same time; per-channel ATP with safety stock is what stops the last unit being sold twice.
alternative: One shared stock number every channel reads.
value: Oversells become rare, and when they happen the customer is offered a backorder, not a cancellation.

decision: Rebalancing applies instantly with a 10-second undo toast, then the allocation service confirms
why: Planners move units dozens of times a day; waiting for a round trip on each is friction, and undo beats a confirmation dialog for reversible actions.
alternative: A confirm dialog and a spinner per move.
value: Fast, forgiving operations, the pattern popularized by email clients.

decision: Cells below safety stock are shaded; a thin bar shows the level without extra columns
why: The matrix is dense by design (HQ merchandising); shading lets the eye find the few cells that need action.
value: Problems are found where they live, in context.

decision: The allocation agent proposes a specific move with its reasoning, and opens the same rebalance form a person uses
why: The agent is fast at spotting the evening-peak pattern; the planner knows the promotion calendar. Sharing one form keeps one set of validations.
alternative: Let the agent move units automatically.
value: The agent saves the analysis, the planner keeps the decision.

decision: Numbers say how fresh they are and drift live from the in-browser world
why: A projection is only useful if you know its age; the simulation makes it live without a streaming backend.
